items.title: Pipeline & delays
items.goal: Every candidate on a job sits in exactly one stage, moved only by a recruiter who types their name. Time limits count Singapore working days and resolve job over client over default. A database view derives on track, due soon and overdue with who the delay is waiting on, and the dashboard shows what needs attention today — with no email anywhere.
prd: Pipeline tracking → Pipeline (approved): seven stages and three end states with no time limit → decided
Pipeline tracking → Time limits (decided): job over client over default; working days Monday to Friday skipping Singapore public holidays → decided
Pipeline tracking → Delay detection 1–4 and 6 → proposed; 5 (delays only on the dashboard, filterable by job owner, no email) → decided
Pipeline tracking → Audit: every stage change stored with the typed recruiter name → decided
Main flows → Delay status: a database view, no scheduled job → suggested
UI design → Pipeline board and Dashboard, both fully usable at phone width → decided
exit: A candidate can be moved between all seven stages and into each end state, and every move writes an audit row with a typed name
Delay status matches hand-worked examples across Fridays, weekends and public holidays
The dashboard lists overdue candidates by days over with filters for client, job, stage and owner
The board and the dashboard are fully usable at 390 px
outOfScope: Any email, reminder or push notification — the portal sends none
AI moving, advancing or rejecting a candidate — the AI only suggests
Scheduled background jobs — Vercel Hobby runs cron once a day, so status is derived in a view
Client or candidate visibility into the pipeline — non-goals

items.title: Recruiters move candidates through stages with an audit trail
items.story: As a recruiter, I want every stage change recorded against the name of whoever made it, so that with no sign-in we can still see who did what.
ac: Given a candidate on a job, when I move them to another stage, then the move is recorded with my typed name and the time.
Given a candidate, when I look at them on a job, then they are in exactly one stage.
Given an end state, when a candidate is moved into it, then no time limit applies to them any more.
Given I have not typed my name on this device, when I try to move anyone, then the portal asks for my name first.
prd: Pipeline tracking → Pipeline (approved): the seven stages and three end states → decided
Pipeline tracking → Audit: stage changes stored in stage_events with the typed recruiter name → decided
Users → the portal asks for a name before a recruiter's first change on a device → decided
Data model → pipeline_entries, stage_events → suggested

items.title: Implement the stage model and the move action with typed-name audit
items.what: Define the seven stages and three end states in code, and implement the move action: it changes the current stage, resets the stage clock and writes an audit row carrying the recruiter's typed name. Test-first.
scope: A single stage definition used by the database, the server and the UI, including which party each stage waits on
A move Server Action validated with Zod, requiring a non-empty typed name

Failing tests first: a move writes one `stage_events` row with the name and time; the stage entry time resets on every move including a move backwards; an end state clears any limit; a move without a name is refused; a candidate never occupies two stages
Adding a candidate to a job creates the entry in Sourced
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the audit row, the clock reset including a backwards move, end states, the missing name and the single-stage rule
The stage list exists once and is used by the database, the server and the UI
No code path moves a candidate without a recruiter action and a typed name

items.title: Delay status is computed from Singapore working days
items.story: As a recruiter, I want the portal to tell me who is running late and by how much, counted the way we actually work, so that I chase the right people on Monday morning.
ac: Given a job limit, a client limit and a default limit, when status is computed, then the job's limit wins, then the client's, then the default.
Given a candidate has used 80% or more of the limit, when status is computed, then they are due soon; past the limit, they are overdue.
Given a candidate in an end state or placed, when status is computed, then they have no delay status at all.
Given a job's limit is changed while candidates sit in that stage, when status is recomputed, then the new limit applies to the running clock.
prd: Pipeline tracking → Time limits (decided): job over client over default; working days skipping Singapore public holidays → decided
Pipeline tracking → Delay detection 1: the clock starts on entering a stage and resets on the next → proposed
Pipeline tracking → Delay detection 2: On track, Due soon at 80%, Overdue → proposed
Pipeline tracking → Delay detection 3: a 'Waiting on' column → proposed
Pipeline tracking → default limit table: Sourced 2, Screening 3, Shortlisted 2, Submitted 5, Client interview 7, Offer 5 → approved in the PRD, to be confirmed with the product owner
Main flows → Delay status derived in a database view → suggested

items.title: Implement limit resolution: job over client over default
items.what: Resolve the working-day limit for a candidate in a stage by taking the job's limit if set, then the client's, then the default. One function, used by the view and by the app. Test-first.
scope: Resolution in SQL for the view and a TypeScript mirror for the app and its tests

Failing tests first: job wins over client and default; client wins over default; default applies when neither is set; a limit explicitly set to zero is honoured rather than treated as unset; an unknown stage fails loudly
A cross-check test that SQL and TypeScript agree
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover all four resolution cases plus the explicit zero
A cross-check proves the SQL and TypeScript resolvers agree
Resolution logic exists in exactly these two mirrored places

items.title: Build the delay-status view: on track, due soon, overdue and waiting on
items.what: Derive delay status in a security-invoker database view from the stage entry time, the resolved limit and the holiday table — no scheduled job, because Vercel Hobby runs cron only once a day. Include days over and who the delay is waiting on. Test-first.
scope: A view returning, per pipeline entry: working days used, the resolved limit, status, days over and the waiting-on party
The due-soon rule at 80% of the limit, with the rounding stated once in the spec and asserted at the boundary

Failing tests first: 79%, exactly 80% and 81%; one day over; entering a stage on a Friday, on a weekend and on the eve of a public holiday; end states and placed return no status; a limit changed mid-stage recomputes rather than using a snapshot
The view is security-invoker so RLS still applies
exclusions: Any cron job or scheduled recompute
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the 80% boundary from both sides, one day over, the Friday, weekend and holiday-eve cases, end states and the mid-stage limit change
The view is security-invoker and returns nothing to the publishable key
Status is derived on read with no scheduled job anywhere in the codebase

items.title: Confirm the default stage limit table with the product owner
items.what: The PRD's stage table was hard to read in the source PDF, and the project skills flagged Screening and Shortlisted as uncertain. A clean text extraction of the PRD reads Sourced 2, Screening 3, Shortlisted 2, Submitted to client 5, Client interview 7, Offer 5. Put those values to the product owner, get a yes or a correction, and only then seed them.
scope: Put the six values and their waiting-on parties to the product owner for confirmation
Record the answer, with its date, in `docs/decisions/open-questions.md`
Seed the confirmed defaults into `stage_limits` at the default level
Update `prd-context/references/pipeline-rules.md` to remove the uncertainty note once confirmed
exclusions: Guessing or silently adopting the values if no answer comes — the register records it as still open instead
Client or job level limits, which recruiters set in Settings
done: The product owner's answer, or the lack of one, is recorded with its date in the open-questions register
Default limits are seeded only for values the owner has confirmed
The uncertainty note in the pipeline rules reference is resolved or left with an explicit reason

items.title: Recruiters work the pipeline board, even on a phone
items.story: As a recruiter standing in a client's lobby, I want to move a candidate on my phone and have it ask for my name, so that the board stays true to reality instead of being updated from memory that evening.
ac: Given the board, when I open it, then there is a column per stage and each candidate shows their delay status as a word or icon as well as colour.
Given I move a candidate, when I confirm, then the portal records my typed name and the candidate's clock resets.
Given I am on a phone at 390 px, when I use the board, then every action is reachable and the page does not scroll horizontally.
Given I use only a keyboard, when I move a candidate, then I can do it without dragging.
prd: UI design → Pipeline board: a column per stage, On track / Due soon / Overdue, typed-name prompt on each move → decided
UI design → design rule 2: status uses a word or icon as well as colour → suggested
UI design → design rule 4: the pipeline board is fully usable at phone width → suggested

items.title: Build the pipeline board with status badges and the typed-name prompt
items.what: Build the board from `design/specs/pipeline.md`: a column per stage, each candidate showing their delay status through the shared badge, moves made by menu or button as well as any drag, and the typed-name prompt on the first move on a device.
scope: The board on job detail and as its own route, reading the delay-status view
`DelayStatusBadge` on every candidate, with end states and placed showing no status
A keyboard-operable move path that does not require dragging
`TypedNameDialog` before the first move on a device
Playwright at both widths: a move works, badges contain words, no horizontal overflow at 390 px
done: A candidate can be moved by keyboard alone, covered by an end-to-end test
Every badge carries a word or icon and an `aria-label`, and end states show no status
The name prompt appears before the first move on a device and not again
Playwright passes at `desktop` and `phone`, including the overflow assertion

items.title: The dashboard shows what needs attention today
items.story: As a recruiter, I want one screen that tells me who is overdue, who is about to be, and which guarantees are ending, so that the absence of email alerts costs me nothing.
ac: Given overdue candidates, when I open the dashboard, then they are listed by days over, most overdue first.
Given the dashboard, when I filter by client, job, stage or owner, then all four filters work and can be combined.
Given a candidate whose delay is with the client, when I look at the list, then the waiting-on party is shown.
Given the dashboard at 390 px, when I use it, then every filter and row is reachable without horizontal scrolling.
prd: Pipeline tracking → Delay detection 4: the dashboard lists overdue candidates by days over, filterable by client, job and stage → proposed
Pipeline tracking → Delay detection 5: delays appear only on the dashboard, filterable by job owner; no email → decided
UI design → Dashboard: overdue and due-soon candidates, guarantee end dates; filters for client, job, stage and owner → decided

items.title: Build the dashboard with overdue, due-soon and guarantee sections and four filters
items.what: Build the dashboard from `design/specs/dashboard.md`: overdue candidates ordered by days over, due-soon candidates, guarantees ending, and filters for client, job, stage and owner — the only place delays surface, because the portal sends no email.
scope: Server-rendered sections reading the delay-status view and the placements guarantee dates
Overdue ordered by days over, with the waiting-on party shown
Four combinable filters, in a sheet at phone width
Empty states that read as good news rather than as errors
Playwright at both widths with the shared assertions
exclusions: Metrics or charts — the four success metrics belong to the real-data release
Changing a candidate's stage from the dashboard, unless the design spec includes it
done: Overdue candidates are ordered by days over and show the waiting-on party
All four filters work individually and combined, covered by an end-to-end test
The guarantee section shows guarantees ending, matching the placements rule
Playwright passes at `desktop` and `phone` including the overflow assertion
